description: This bar chart, from the paper "Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets," illustrates the GPU memory consumption in gigabytes (GB) for various fine-tuning methods. The vertical axis, labeled "GPU Memory (GB)", is scaled linearly from 0 to 60, with major gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 20. The horizontal axis lists the methods being compared: "Full FT", "MTL-FT", "TAG", "LoRA", "QLoRA", and "Ours". Each method is represented by a single bar. The "Full FT" method consumes the most memory, with a bar reaching approximately 70 GB, which is visually taller than the 60 GB gridline. The "MTL-FT" method uses about 40 GB. The "TAG", "LoRA", and "QLoRA" methods each use approximately 20 GB. The "Ours" method, represented by a green bar, uses about 20 GB. The "Full FT" bar is the tallest, followed by "MTL-FT", then the three methods using approximately 20 GB each, with "Ours" being the shortest among them. The bars are arranged in descending order of memory usage from left to right, and the "Ours" bar is the only one colored green, while all others are orange.
